question: Which physical feature marks the northeastern boundary of the Peninsular Block?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Malda Fault**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Malda Fault is a significant geological feature located in the northeastern region of the Peninsular Block of India.
 
• It separates the Peninsular Block from the younger Himalayan foredeep and marks the transition zone between two tectonic provinces.
 
• The Malda Fault is associated with seismic activity due to its role in the interaction between the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate.
 
• This fault line is characterized by tectonic disturbances, making the region geologically complex.
 
• The area near the Malda Fault is known for its unique geomorphological features and serves as a boundary for the Peninsular Block.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peninsular Block of India:**

 
 
• The Peninsular Block is the oldest and most stable landmass of India, composed primarily of Precambrian rocks.
 
• It is bounded by several geological features, including the Aravalli Hills, Eastern Ghats, and Western Ghats.
 
• This region forms the Deccan Plateau and is tectonically stable compared to the Himalayan region.
 
 
 
• **Faults in Geology:**
 
 
• A fault is a fracture or zone of fractures between two blocks of rock.
 
• Faults allow the blocks to move relative to each other, causing earthquakes and changes in the landscape.
 
• They are classified into normal, reverse, and strike-slip faults based on their movement.
 
 
 
• **Seismic Zones of India:**
 
 
• India is divided into four seismic zones based on earthquake risks: Zone II, III, IV, and V.
 
• The northeastern region, including areas near the Malda Fault, falls under high-risk zones (Zone IV and V).
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Foredeep:**
 
 
• The Himalayan Foredeep is a structural depression formed by the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate.
 
• It is a sedimentary basin located south of the Himalayan Range.
 
• This region is tectonically active, contributing to frequent seismic activity.
